ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Howard Hughes

code.originalText: One-week review, seen the same day by psychiatry: the diagnosis of OCD, an SSRI, exposure and response prevention, and starting buprenorphine

text.paragraph: One-week review of contamination fears and codeine use, seen the same day by psychiatry. [S]

Mr. Hughes returns one week after intake and is seen by Dr. Bachmann-Adeyemi of psychiatry on the same day. He took his last acetaminophen-codeine tablet about 20 hours ago, as planned for starting buprenorphine today, and has taken no more than the prescribed eight tablets a day this week. He has yawning, aching, a runny nose and gooseflesh. The contamination fears and washing are unchanged, at about four hours a day; he washed his hands eleven times before coming in. He completed the PCL-5 about the crash. The intake urine test, done with his consent, was positive for codeine and morphine, as expected, and negative for fentanyl, other opioids, benzodiazepines and other drugs. The prescription monitoring report showed acetaminophen-codeine from two prescribers at two pharmacies and no other controlled drugs. HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests were negative; he is not immune to hepatitis B. He has taken his unused codeine tablets to a pharmacy take-back. [S]

Intrusive fears of contamination by germs for about a year, worse since the crash, with hand washing, cleaning of objects and avoidance of handshakes, shared spaces and food handled by others, taking about four hours a day; he recognizes the fears are probably excessive; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented fear of germs; resolved into the diagnosis of OCD at the consultation. Not a claim about his real symptoms in 1947.

list.item:
Obsessive-compulsive disorder, contamination type, with good or fair insight (F42.2). Dr. Bachmann-Adeyemi confirms obsessive-compulsive disorder with good or fair insight: the obsessions are unwanted and intrusive, the washing and avoidance are aimed at preventing contamination, and they take about four hours a day. It is not obsessive-compulsive personality disorder, illness anxiety disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PCL-5 18) or a psychotic disorder. Y-BOCS 28, severe. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Sertraline 50 mg daily, with a plan to raise the dose every four to six weeks toward 200 mg.
Exposure and response prevention with the clinic psychologist, weekly 90-minute sessions, starting next week.
With his written consent, his personal assistant will join two therapy sessions to learn how staff can stop carrying out rituals for him.

Opioid use disorder, moderate (F11.20). COWS 13 about 20 hours after the last codeine dose, so buprenorphine can start without precipitating withdrawal. He chose buprenorphine after hearing the options, including a slow codeine taper. [S]
Buprenorphine with naloxone 4 mg in the clinic, a further 4 mg two hours later, and up to 4 mg more this evening if needed; 8 mg twice daily from tomorrow.
Dispensed one week at a time; naloxone at home.
No benzodiazepines.

Chronic pain after major trauma (G89.21). Codeine combination tablets have stopped, so acetaminophen is given on a schedule instead. [S]
Acetaminophen 1,000 mg three times daily, no more than 3,000 mg a day.
Physical therapy for the chest wall, left shoulder and low back, twice weekly.

Weight loss (R63.4). Weight 72.3 kg; he eats one meal a day that he has watched being made. [S]
Dietitian visit next week; meals will become part of the exposure plan.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (2007); Guideline Watch (March 2013): Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (Koran LM, Simpson HB), as reported by Psychiatric News (2013); Obsessive-compulsive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder: treatment (CG31) (2005); CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain - United States, 2022 (2022); The ASAM National Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Opioid Use Disorder: 2020 Focused Update (2020); Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs (PDMPs) (2026); Hearing loss in adults: assessment and management (NG98) (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026)

Follow-up: Telephone check tomorrow after the second day of buprenorphine. Five-week review with the audiogram that morning. Call the clinic or 988 at any time; use naloxone and call 911 for heavy sleepiness or slow breathing. Next scheduled visit 2026-06-08: five-week review: OCD treatment, buprenorphine, pain, the audiogram and weight. [S]
